question: Why is immense material wealth insufficient compared to the value of this teaching?
premises: A hypothetical accumulation vast enough to fill the ocean with jewels is imagined.
Such wealth represents extreme material abundance.
The comparison implies something surpasses even that.
inference: Even wealth enough to fill the ocean with jewels is not comparable to this teaching.
uncertainties: The fused form ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is difficult and may contain a scribal irregularity.
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels...
